title: Double-entry bookkeeping survived because it makes error detection local
content: Double-entry bookkeeping survived for six centuries while other accounting systems did not because it makes error detection local: every transaction touches two accounts, so a mistake shows up as an imbalance rather than as a wrong total nobody notices.

source_refs.quote: Today we look at why double-entry bookkeeping survived for six centuries while other accounting systems did not.
The short answer is that it makes error detection local. Every transaction touches two accounts, so a mistake shows up as an imbalance rather than as a wrong total nobody notices.

attribution.note: Preserved the causal claim as the lecturer's explanation, not as an externally verified fact.

review.note: The lecturer states a reason for the survival of double-entry bookkeeping; kept the condition that errors surface as imbalances.
